code.originalText: Eight-week stroke and blood pressure review with lipid panel and rhythm-monitor results

text.paragraph: Eight-week stroke and blood pressure review. [S]

Mr. Churchill returns eight weeks after his stroke and three weeks after the sick visit at which amlodipine was reduced to 5 mg for orthostatic lightheadedness. The lightheadedness resolved within two days, and his home standing pressures have been 120 to 130 systolic. He has had no falls and no new neurological symptoms. He walks outdoors without a stick and his handwriting is nearly normal. He has started chairing meetings at work again, for half days. The 30-day heart monitor was returned five days ago. He is down to about four cigars a day and no longer drinks in the afternoon. His mood is better and he cries less often. [S]
